land.text: Assur, the city that became an independent city-state under Puzur-Ashur I

predecessors.note: The Assyria page infobox lists the Third Dynasty of Ur as predecessor; the page gives the city, not a territory.

land.text: the Assyrian heartland of Cliopatria's last Assyria shape, from which the Neo-Assyrian Empire expands

successors.note: Same state: the Middle Assyrian Empire ends with the death of Ashur-dan II in 912 and the page counts the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 911 (accession of Adad-nirari II). Cliopatria switches rows at -900.

capitals.name: Šubat-Enlil (Tell Leilan)
capitals.note: Shamshi-Adad I made the former Shekhna "the capital city of Assyria" and renamed it Šubat-Enlil c. 1808; the Assyria infobox keeps Assur throughout.

capitals.name: Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta (Tulul al-Aqar)
capitals.note: Founded "in the eleventh year of his reign (c. 1233 BC)"; the infobox gives Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta c. 1233-1207. About 3 km upstream of Assur; coordinates approximate.

correction.text: the independent city-state of Assur under Puzur-Ashur I and his successors; the trade network ("a hub in a large trading network that spanned from the Zagros Mountains in the east") is not territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in -1800 but the page gives an independent city-state of Assur from c. 2025 BC, trading from Kanesh to the Zagros. The page names no territory, so the shape is the city and its fields.

correction.text: Assur and Ekallatum on the Tigris and Subat-Enlil (the former Shekhna, Tell Leilan) on the Khabur plain: the places the page ties to Shamshi-Adad I before his later conquests

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Shamshi-Adad I takes Assur (c. 1808 per the Assyria and Old Assyrian pages; c. 1809 per his page) and makes Shekhna (Tell Leilan) his capital Subat-Enlil c. 1808; Cliopatria's shape begins only in -1800.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Upper Mesopotamian shape of Shamshi-Adad I's kingdom without the stray cell in Thrace

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 77,171 km2 (-1800..-1761) is the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia ("eventually came to include most of northern Mesopotamia"); one stray cell at 27.7 E 41.03 N (Eastern Thrace) lies 1,500 km from the rest and is removed. The page gives no area. The shape stops at the Euphrates side of the Khabur, so Shamshi-Adad I's claim to Syria and Anatolia ("much of Syria, Anatolia", Shamshi-Adad I page) is left out.

correction.text: the Assur core without the stray cell in Thrace

keyframe_review.note: 25,617 km2: the Assur core after the kingdom's collapse (c. 1776) and Hammurabi's conquest of "the region" c. 1761, when he "appears to have respected Assur and its institutions". The same stray cell at 27.7 E 41.03 N is removed.

correction.text: Cliopatria's -1700 shape without the stray cell in Thrace; extent not on the page

keyframe_review.note: 63,722 km2 for the Adaside dynasty (Bel-bani c. 1700-1691): the page says nothing about an expansion from the 25,617 km2 core. Shape kept apart from the stray Thracian cell at 27.7 E 41.03 N; the extent is unverified (page silent).

35,816 km2 around Assur-Tikrit-Kirkuk for the Mitanni years: "Around c. 1430 BC, Assur was subjugated by Mitanni and forced to become a vassal" until c. 1360. The page does not say that Assyria lost land in -1500, 70 years before; the vassalage belongs to Mitanni's dossier (vassal_start counterpart assyria).
34,429 km2: the core under Mitanni to c. 1360; independence follows under Ashur-uballit I (c. 1363). The shape does not change at 1363; the growth is the next shape.

195,097 km2 (-1300..-1241): Ashur-uballit I's conquests of "the fertile region between the Tigris, the foothills of the Taurus Mountains and the Upper Zab", Adad-nirari I's cities on the Khabur and the lands of Mitanni; the pages give no area. Within the range the pages support.

445,831 km2: Shalmaneser I's annexation of Hanigalbat and Tukulti-Ninurta I's early conquests ("brought the Middle Assyrian Empire to its greatest extent"). The page names no frontier or area; the Nihriya victory over the Hittites c. 1237 gives no land.

correction.text: Assyria's own lands in the last years of Tukulti-Ninurta I and after: Cliopatria's -1220 shape without Babylonia, which the babylonia dossier supplies as a vassal from 1225 and as an independent Kassite state from 1216

keyframe_review.note: 599,270 km2 (-1220..-1201), Cliopatria's maximum, includes all of Babylonia down to the Gulf (29.5 N). The pages say Babylonia was conquered c. 1225 and "became an Assyrian vassal c. 1225-1216 BC"; Adad-shuma-usur "drove the Assyrians out c. 1216 BC". Babylonia is therefore a vassal (lighter tint) 1225-1217 and free from 1216, not Assyrian land; Cliopatria also has no Babylonia shape -1220..-1201. The corrected shape is Assyria without the Babylonian shape of -1240.

467,282 km2: after Tukulti-Ninurta I's murder (c. 1207) the page records "inter-dynastic conflict and a significant drop in Assyrian power" but dates no territorial loss before the decline of 1055-935; Cliopatria's -1200 shape stays at 467,282 km2. Unverified in detail: page silent on frontiers 1207-1115.

515,451 km2: Ashur-dan I (c. 1178-1133), Ashur-resh-ishi I (1132-1115) and Tiglath-Pileser I (1114-1076), whose armies reached the Mediterranean and "conquered 42 lands" (Tiglath-Pileser page); the page also calls the conquests "ephemeral and shaky, quickly lost again".

correction.text: unchanged, but valid only for -1100..-1056; from -1055 the heartland shape applies

keyframe_review.note: 515,080 km2 is right only to 1056. "Second period of decline: 1055-935 BC" (infobox): after Ashur-bel-kala (d. 1056) the empire lost "most of the empire's territories outside of its heartlands, partly due to invasions by Aramean tribes", and "By 1000 BC, Assyria was at the low point of its power". Use this shape for -1100..-1056 and the heartland shape (new keyframe assyria_-1055) after.

correction.text: the Assyrian heartland around Assur, Nineveh and Arbela that "continued to remain intact"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1055..-1001: the heartland after the loss of "most of the empire's territories outside of its heartlands" (the decline dated 1055-935 in the infobox). Cliopatria changes at -1000; the page dates the loss from the death of Ashur-bel-kala in 1056.

correction.text: unchanged, valid -1000..-912; -911..-901 belong to the neo-assyrian-empire dossier

keyframe_review.note: 25,473 km2: the heartland through Ashur-dan II (934-912), who reversed the decline by campaigning "in the northeast and northwest". Page silent on the lands he recovered; the Cliopatria row runs -1000..-901 but this dossier ends in -912 and the Neo-Assyrian Empire dossier begins in -911, so the shape is valid only to -912.

region.text: the city-state of Assur

ledger.note: c. 2025 BC: Assur becomes an independent city-state under Puzur-Ashur I. "Assur is generally thought to have become an independent city-state under Puzur-Ashur I, who ruled c. 2025 BC" (Old Assyrian period); the Assyria infobox "Assur becomes an independent city-state: c. 2025 BC". The page gives the city, not a boundary.

c. 1808 BC: the Amorite Shamshi-Adad I takes Assur and founds a new dynasty. "The original Assur city-state, and the Puzur-Ashur dynasty, came to an end c. 1808 BC when the city was conquered by the Amorite ruler of Ekallatum"; his own page has c. 1809 and the Old Assyrian page "c. 1808 BC".

c. 1808 BC: Shamshi-Adad I moves the capital to Subat-Enlil. He "converted it [Shekhna, today Tell Leilan] into the capital city of Assyria, and then renamed it Šubat-Enlil" c. 1808 BC; the court had been at Ekallatum. The Assyria infobox keeps Assur.

region.text: Shekhna, today Tell Leilan, renamed Subat-Enlil

ledger.note: c. 1808 BC: Shekhna on the Khabur plain becomes the royal seat. The page dates the conversion of Shekhna into Subat-Enlil to c. 1808 BC and says nothing of its prior ruler.

region.text: most of northern Mesopotamia between the Tigris and the Euphrates, Cliopatria's Upper Mesopotamian shape

ledger.counterpart: Amorite and Hurrian city-states of Upper Mesopotamia
ledger.note: The Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia: the pages date no conquest except Mari. The Old Assyrian page says the kingdom "eventually came to include most of northern Mesopotamia" and Shamshi-Adad I's page that he "had conquered lands across much of Syria, Anatolia, and Upper Mesopotamia"; the date -1800 is Cliopatria's first shape, not the page's.

region.text: Mari on the middle Euphrates, with Yasmah-Adad on the throne

ledger.note: c. 1796 BC: Shamshi-Adad I occupies Mari. "Shamshi-Adad I seized the opportunity and occupied Mari around 1796 BC" and "put his second son, Yasmah-Adad, on the throne in Mari"; Mari stays a separate kingdom under his son, so this is a gain by the royal house.

region.text: Upper Mesopotamia outside the Assur core, Mari and Subat-Enlil: the coalition of Andarig, Eshnunna and others took the rest (Mari and Subat-Enlil have their own events)

ledger.counterpart: coalition of Mari, Andarig and Eshnunna
ledger.note: c. 1776 BC: Shamshi-Adad I dies and the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia breaks up. "Shamshi-Adad's death c. 1776 BC led to the collapse of the kingdom"; his page: "Yasmah-Adad was soon expelled from Mari by Zimri-Lim" and "the rest of the kingdom was eventually lost during the reigns of Ishme-Dagan I and Mut-Ashkur" to "a coalition of Mari, Andarig, and Eshnunna". Ishme-Dagan I "retained control only of Ekallatum" (dying c. 1765). The pages give no year for the individual losses; all land beyond the Assur core goes at the collapse, except Mari (own event, same year) and Subat-Enlil (held until Eshnunna seized it c. 1772). Counterpart corrected by reviewer me-02 from "eshnunna": the Shamshi-Adad I page has the kingdom lost "first to a coalition of Mari, Andarig, and Eshnunna", and eshnunna books no gain here.

region.text: Mari on the middle Euphrates, with Yasmah-Adad on the throne

ledger.note: c. 1776 BC: Zimri-Lim expels Yasmah-Adad from Mari. Shamshi-Adad I's page: "Yasmah-Adad was soon expelled from Mari by Zimri-Lim" after the king's death c. 1776 BC; the Mari page puts Zimri-Lim's enthronement at c. 1776 BC (the Zimri-Lim page, c. 1775).

region.text: Subat-Enlil (Shubat-Enlil, former Shekhna, Tell Leilan), Shamshi-Adad's old capital

ledger.note: c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna seizes Subat-Enlil. "In c. 1772 BC, the new king of Eshnunna, Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom, occupying Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare before seizing Shamshi-Adad's old capital at Shubut-Enlil." (Old Assyrian period).

region.text: Assur, Ekallatum and Qattara

ledger.note: c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna occupies Assur. "Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom" and took "Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare" (c. 1772 BC); the Shamshi-Adad I page has only "Eshnunna captured cities around Assur".

region.text: Assur, Ekallatum and Qattara

ledger.note: c. 1767 BC (bridged): the Eshnunna occupation of Assur ends. The Old Assyrian page does not say when Eshnunna left ("Assur at some point returned to being an independent city-state"; Hammurabi "conquered the region c. 1761 BC"); the Eshnunna page has Elam conquering Eshnunna around 1767 (Ibal-pi-El II killed c. 1765), and Ishme-Dagan I (d. c. 1765) "retained control only of Ekallatum". The end is bridged to the Elamite conquest of Eshnunna.

region.text: the hinterland of Assur added in Cliopatria's -1700 shape; no page names it

ledger.note: The heartland widens from 25,617 km2 to 63,722 km2 in Cliopatria's -1700 shape, when "Bel-bani founded the Adaside dynasty" (c. 1700-1691); the page names no conquest. Recorded to explain the shape change, at confidence 1.

region.text: the parts of the -1700 shape outside the Assur-Kirkuk core

ledger.note: Cliopatria shrinks the shape at -1500 (63,722 to 35,816 km2), 70 years before the page's Mitanni date. The land lost is the north and south of the old heartland; Mitanni's first shape begins in -1500 and reaches 38.2 N. Page silent on the year and the land.

c. 1363 BC: Ashur-uballit I makes Assyria a territorial state again. "Assyria became an independent territorial state under Ashur-uballit I c. 1363 BC, having previously been under the suzerainty of the Mitanni kingdom" (Mitanni's hold from c. 1430). The Middle Assyrian period begins.

region.text: the fertile region between the Tigris, the foothills of the Taurus Mountains and the Upper Zab

ledger.note: c. 1363 BC: Ashur-uballit I conquers "the fertile region between the Tigris, the foothills of the Taurus Mountains and the Upper Zab", which "modern historians use to mark the beginning of the Middle Assyrian period". Arrapha and Nuzi were attacked (Nuzi destroyed "in the 1330s BC or before") but "neither city was formally incorporated into Assyria".

region.text: several cities alongside the Khabur river

ledger.note: Adad-nirari I (c. 1305-1274) "annexed several cities alongside the Khabur river" after Wasashatta's revolt. The page gives no year; -1300 is Cliopatria's shape change.

region.text: the remnant of Mitanni (Hanigalbat) between the Khabur and the Balikh; Washukanni sacked

ledger.note: Shalmaneser I (c. 1273-1244) takes the last of Mitanni. "Under Shalmaneser I, the last remnants of the Mitanni kingdom were formally annexed into Assyria" (Assyria page); the Middle Assyrian page: "The lands were not annexed directly into the royal domains, rather placed under the rule of a viceroy who bore the title of grand vizier and king of Hanigalbat". Neither gives a year; -1244 is the last year of his reign.

region.text: the conquests beyond the old frontier in Cliopatria's -1240 shape (north and east of the old heartland); the page says only "wide-ranging conquests"

ledger.counterpart: the northern and eastern neighbours of Assyria (page silent)
ledger.note: Tukulti-Ninurta I (c. 1243-1207) "brought the Middle Assyrian Empire to its greatest extent". The pages name no lands but Babylonia; the growth between Cliopatria's -1300 and -1240 shapes beyond Hanigalbat is the north (Armenian highlands) and east (Zagros). Page silent on which lands.

region.text: Babylonia, which became an Assyrian vassal

ledger.note: c. 1225 BC: Tukulti-Ninurta I conquers Babylonia and takes Kashtiliash IV prisoner. "his temporary conquest of Babylonia, which became an Assyrian vassal c. 1225-1216 BC" (Assyria page); "conquering Babylonia c. 1225 BC" (Middle Assyrian page).

region.text: Babylonia, vassal c. 1225-1216

ledger.note: c. 1216 BC: Babylonia throws off Assyria. A revolt of Adad-shuma-iddina "c. 1217 BC", then Adad-shuma-usur "drove the Assyrians out c. 1216 BC". Cliopatria wrongly keeps Babylonia inside the Assyria shape to -1201.

c. 1207 BC: Tukulti-Ninurta I is murdered and the court returns from Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta (capital c. 1233-1207) to Assur (infobox "Assur (c. 1207–912 BC)"). "The assassination of Tukulti-Ninurta I c. 1207 BC led to inter-dynastic conflict and a significant decline in Assyrian power."

region.text: everything outside the Assyrian heartland: the -1220 shape (without Babylonia) minus the heartland shape of -1000

ledger.note: c. 1206 BC: first period of decline. Infobox: "First period of decline: c. 1206–1115 BC"; after Tukulti-Ninurta I's murder (c. 1207) "Assyria became restricted mostly to just the Assyrian heartland." The loss is dated to 1206, six years before the -1200 keyframe (assyria_-1200, whose window-patch override m1200-m1101 keyframe_overrides/3 draws the heartland from -1200 to -1115), so the empire shape of -1220 does not run on to -1201. Fixes request R021; the keyframes and the -1150 cancelling loss stay in the patch (it controls them).

region.text: the western addition of Cliopatria's -1150 shape toward the Euphrates and Syria

ledger.note: Cliopatria's shape widens westward at -1150 (467,282 to 515,451 km2, west edge from 36.4 E to 34.9 E). Tiglath-Pileser I (1114-1076) reached the Mediterranean and Malatya, but the page dates no conquest in -1150; the shape change is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Commagene and the upper Euphrates lands taken from the Mushki; "Anatolia, Levant and Ancient Iran, and to the shores of the Mediterranean Sea"

ledger.note: 1112 BC: Tiglath-Pileser I fights the Mushki and overruns Commagene. "His first campaign was against the Phrygians (Mushku) in 1112 BC ... then he overran Commagene and Cappadocia" and "drove the Hittites from the Assyrian ruled Hurrian province of Subartu"; the Middle Assyrian page: he "defeated the Mushki, a tribe who had taken control of various lands in the north fifty years prior". Years for later campaigns (Lake Van, Malatya, Byblos, Sidon, Arvad) are not on the page.

region.text: everything outside the heartland: Cliopatria's -1100 shape without its -1000 shape

ledger.note: 1055 BC: Assyria falls back to its heartland. "Second period of decline: 1055-935 BC" (infobox): after Ashur-bel-kala (d. 1056) the empire lost "most of the empire's territories outside of its heartlands, partly due to invasions by Aramean tribes". Eriba-Adad II (r. 1056-1054) is the first king of the "intensified" decline. The page dates the loss to the period, not a year.

region.text: the heartland; no lands regained are named on the page

ledger.note: 934 BC: Ashur-dan II begins the recovery. "Assyrian decline began to be reversed again under Ashur-dan II (r. 934-912 BC)", who "campaigned in the northeast and northwest". The page names no land; Cliopatria's shape shows the heartland to -901 and the Neo-Assyrian page (neo-assyrian-empire dossier) carries the reconquest.

region.text: the Assyrian heartland handed to the Neo-Assyrian Empire

ledger.note: 912 BC: the Middle Assyrian Empire ends with the death of Ashur-dan II; the Neo-Assyrian Empire is counted from 911 (accession of Adad-nirari II). Same state, same family: successor in the next dossier.

wars.name: Shamshi-Adad I's conquests (Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia)
wars.outcome: Shamshi-Adad I took Assur c. 1808, Mari c. 1796 and built the kingdom; it collapsed after his death c. 1776.
wars.note: Allied with Dadusha of Eshnunna to conquer the area between the two Zabs c. 1781, then "later turned against Dadusha" (Shaduppum, Nerebtum, Andarig); the page gives no year for the later war.

wars.name: Eshnunna's invasion of Ishme-Dagan I's kingdom
wars.outcome: Ibal-pi-el II of Eshnunna occupied Assur, Ekallatum and Qattara.

wars.name: Hammurabi's conquest of northern Mesopotamia
wars.outcome: Hammurabi of Babylon "conquered the region c. 1761 BC" but "appears to have respected Assur and its institutions".

wars.name: Mitanni's subjugation of Assur
wars.outcome: Assur became a Mitanni vassal c. 1430 and regained independence under Ashur-uballit I c. 1363; no land is named. Vassal record belongs to the mitanni dossier.

wars.name: Adad-nirari I's Khabur campaigns
wars.outcome: Wasashatta, son of Shattuara, rebelled and was defeated; Adad-nirari I annexed several cities on the Khabur.
wars.note: Years are his reign (c. 1305-1274); the page does not date the war. A victory over Babylon at Kar-Ishtar is dated "c. 1280 BC" without a territorial result.

wars.name: Shalmaneser I's conquest of Hanigalbat
wars.outcome: After Shattuara II rebelled with Hittite help, Shalmaneser I sacked Washukanni and the remnant of Mitanni passed to Assyria.
wars.note: Years are his reign (c. 1273-1244); neither page dates the campaign.

wars.name: Battle of Nihriya
wars.outcome: Tukulti-Ninurta I "defeated the Hittites at the Battle of Nihriya c. 1237 BC"; the page gives no land and no treaty.

wars.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I's conquest of Babylonia

zones.text: Babylonia, taken c. 1225 and lost c. 1216

wars.outcome: Kashtiliash IV was taken prisoner; Babylonia was an Assyrian vassal c. 1225-1216 until Adad-shuma-usur drove the Assyrians out.

wars.name: Assyro-Babylonian wars under Ashur-resh-ishi I and Tiglath-Pileser I
wars.outcome: Ashur-resh-ishi I fought Nebuchadnezzar I over Zanqi; Tiglath-Pileser I attacked Babylon but "did not conquer Babylonia"; Ashur-bel-kala's dispute with Marduk-nadin-ahhe was "resolved diplomatically".
wars.note: Years are the reigns; the page dates none of the fighting.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser I's campaigns

zones.text: Commagene and Cappadocia, Malatya, the mountains south of Lake Van and the Mediterranean coast (Byblos, Sidon, Arvad)

wars.outcome: Conquests from the Mushki (1112) to the Mediterranean; "ephemeral and shaky, quickly lost again" and the end of the reign a "period of retrenchment".
wars.note: Only the 1112 Mushki campaign is dated on the page.

wars.name: Aramean invasions and the second decline
wars.outcome: Assyria lost "most of the empire's territories outside of its heartlands", partly to Aramean tribes; by 1000 BC it was "at the low point of its power"; Ashur-dan II began the recovery from 934.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier appears on the pages for any period: city-state hinterland, an Amorite kingdom, a vassal of Mitanni, and a conquest empire whose edges are approximate.

notes:
SPLIT AND IDENTITY. Cliopatria's Assyria row (-1800..-901) is one state in two parts in this batch: assyria (c. 2025 to 912, Assur city-state, Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia, Middle Assyrian Empire) and neo-assyrian-empire (911 to 609). The Assyria article treats them as one continuous state, so the colour agent may give both one colour; their dossiers are separate only because Cliopatria has two rows and the orchestrator assigned two. Wikidata Q41137 is shared with the row "Syria" (1973..2024), the modern republic: a wrong id on that row, not the same state. The -1800 start is Cliopatria's; the dossier starts in -2025 (page).
CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO CORRECT. A stray cell at 27.7 E 41.03 N (Eastern Thrace) is part of the -1800, -1760 and -1700 shapes (removed by intersect). The -1220 shape holds all of Babylonia although the pages say vassal 1225-1216 and independent after. The -1100 shape runs 45 years too long (loss of the territories from 1055). No Assyria shape for -2025..-1801.
PAGES. 5 pages (budget 5): Assyria, Middle Assyrian Empire (three queries), Shamshi-Adad I, Old Assyrian period, Tiglath-Pileser I. No infobox gives an area, so no area comparison was possible; shape areas stand on the pages' verbal extents only. Not opened for budget: Tukulti-Ninurta I, Shalmaneser I, Adad-nirari I, Mitanni, Aramean kingdoms; hence the confidence-1 events at -1700, -1500, -1300, -1244, -1243, -1150, -934.
DISAGREEMENTS. Hanigalbat: Assyria page "formally annexed" vs Middle Assyrian page "not annexed directly ... viceroy ... king of Hanigalbat" (drawn as Assyrian land with this note). Shamshi-Adad took Assur c. 1809 (his page) or c. 1808 (Assyria, Old Assyrian pages). Capital: the Assyria infobox keeps Assur while Shamshi-Adad I's page makes Subat-Enlil the capital c. 1808.
FOR OTHER DOSSIERS. mitanni (me-04) should carry vassal_start counterpart assyria c. -1430 and vassal_end -1363 (Old Assyrian period page), and the loss of Hanigalbat to Assyria (-1244 here, confidence 1). babylonia (this batch) carries the vassal mirror. eshnunna and lim-dynasty-of-mari are written in this batch (mirrors: loss of Mari -1776 and of Subat-Enlil -1772, the Eshnunna occupation of Assur -1772 to -1767; the Mari gain -1796 is the Assur-side view of the lim dossier's wider loss); Ekallatum and Qattara have no known coordinates. The occupation end was bridged to -1767 (the Elamite conquest of Eshnunna, eshnunna page) instead of Hammurabi's c. 1761, which only ends Eshnunna's independence in -1762.
GAZETTEER. Names used that the gazetteer lacks: Subat-Enlil / Tell Leilan (36.96 N, 41.50 E, used as a coordinate), Mari (used as a coordinate 34.55 N, 40.89 E), Ekallatum (unlocated). Region "Assyria" in the gazetteer is the Assur-Nineveh-Arbela heartland (114,311 km2).
RULERS omitted: the pages give reign years for only part of the kings, so no continuous strip.
